generated_registries.description: Generated registry view for standard cx.* Event.kind values and wire scopes.

generated_registries.description: Generated registry view for active schema IDs and schema file locations.

generated_registries.description: Generated registry view for cx:<kind>: typed ID prefixes and storage/wire rules.

wire_scope_definitions.durable_event: Valid Event Envelope kind for persisted canonical history and reducer input.
wire_scope_definitions.actor_private_event: Persisted actor-private/account-data event; not shared Realm history and not Realm reducer input.
wire_scope_definitions.ephemeral_event: Transient sync/federation/app signal; MUST NOT be persisted as durable Event Envelope history.

registry_rules: Standard cx.* effect kinds MUST appear in this registry when used by a Move effect or Event Envelope payload router.

Events API, Sync durable history, Federation, and canonical reducers MUST accept only active entries with wire_scope=durable_event unless an implementation profile explicitly defines a private channel for actor_private_event.
Entries with wire_scope=ephemeral_event MUST be carried only on ephemeral channels and MUST NOT advance Anchor frontier, Move state_root, or reducer state.
Entries with wire_scope=actor_private_event MAY be persisted in encrypted account data or an actor-private stream, but MUST NOT be inserted into a shared Realm Move/Anchor history.

Reducer-input durable kinds MAY declare cell_family, cell_subject, lattice, bottom, and (cas_register only) initial_value. cell_family is a stable cx.component.*.v<n> URI; cell_subject is null, a payload field path, or a composite descriptor; bottom is reject or expose. initial_value declares the value the cas_register reports before any Move has been applied; declaring `initial_value="__unset__"` combined with `head_eq:"__unset__"` Move predicates implements singleton-once-set cells.

Lattice MUST be one of: core types or_set, mv_register, cas_register, fsm, counter, ordered_log; or extension types lww_register, rga (only declarable on cells with cell_role in {ui_affordance, content, draft, cosmetic} and only valid for receivers that implement cx.profile.collaborative_text.v1; receivers without that profile MUST fail closed with unsupported_lattice_type when an event_kind references a cell using lww_register or rga). Authorization, policy, anchorer, membership, and lifecycle cells MUST NOT use lww_register or rga.

State convergence is defined by Move preconditions/effects, Anchor DAG finality, and per-cell Lattice join. Compatibility Event Envelope fields are payload routing only and MUST NOT be used as ordering authority.

payload_schema_contract.validation_rule: Every active standard cx.* event kind MUST be validated by the Event Envelope schema and one payload class selected by kind. Unknown standard kind, unmatched active kind, or payload class failure is schema_violation before reducer execution.
payload_schema_contract.non_critical_extension_rule: Unknown non-critical payload fields are preserved in canonical bytes and MAY be ignored by reducers. Unknown critical payload semantics MUST be declared in Event.requirements.critical_extensions and fail closed when unsupported.

event_kinds.payload: Realm official or sponsoring organization statement

Typed Realm link graph edge. link_kind declares governance / discoverability / import-export / confidential-extension semantics; it is never generic parent/child containment and never implicitly propagates membership, capabilities, history, E2EE keys, retention, or federation policy.
Enabled Realm policy components set. Payload MUST carry monotonic policy_revision; reducer rejects rollback or gaps and policy_frontier_hash MUST cover policy_revision.

Constraints on member delivery_binding: which binding_source values are admissible, which recipient services are allowed, which endorsers are required, whether DID Document fallback / unroutable membership are permitted, who may sign rebind. Governs reducer acceptance of cx.member.state{membership=join}.delivery_binding (see governance/join-policy.md §5.1).

Realm read receipt disclosure policy (disclosure / visibility / scope_overrides_allowed / allow_child_privacy_tightening_against_required); see zh/discovery/read-receipts.md §2.5 for the compliance-floor escape switch
Realm moderation policy (blocklists, allowlists, content filters)
Plaintext-visible services declaration outside E2EE boundary
Per-parent inheritance policy; one entry per source Realm
Realm tombstone lifecycle facet (terminal pointer to successor)
Realm destroy lifecycle facet (terminal decommission marker)

Issuer-signed endorsement that a subject DID (typically an agent / service / hosted actor) is accountable_to the issuer for a declared scope (employment / contracted_service / agent_operator / etc.). Required to verify `Actor Profile.accountable_to[]` entries; reducer strips unverified DIDs from accountable_to. See zh/models/actor.md §3.3.1.

Flow business-progression stage transition. Single source of truth for mutating Flow.stage / Flow.stage_changed_at; cx.flow.update patch on those paths MUST be rejected (forbidden-wire). The payload intentionally carries no reason / note / explanation field — rationale belongs in a Message on the Flow's discussion track that 'references' this event, and the event log's own actor_id / created_at is the audit source. Reducer enforces hard invariants from zh/models/common-fields.md §5.3.3: state=redacted yields failed_precondition reason=flow_already_terminal; state=archived yields flow_not_active; same-value self-transition is accepted but does NOT update stage_changed_at; reducer overwrites any wire-supplied stage_changed_at with the event's created_at. A per-Realm workflow profile MAY narrow which transitions are legal beyond these hard invariants.

Unified Flow tracks patch. payload.patch uses cx.patch.v1 against the Flow.tracks map: keys are track names (e.g. `synthesis`, `discussion`), values are patch ops that may toggle enabled, set is_primary, or modify profile / fields on a track entry. Atomic across multiple tracks.

Flow move between Spaces (target_space_id in payload). Writes a cas_register cell keyed by (board_space_id, flow_id); the contains Relation list_space_id->flow_id is derived from cell value, not a separate truth source.
Flow reorder within Space. Writes the same cell as cx.flow.move; effect.list_space_id MUST equal head_eq.list_space_id (rank-only update).

Set or clear a per-(flow, actor) watch subscription. Writes a cas_register cell keyed by (flow_id, watcher_actor_id). Payload carries level in {mentions_only, participating, all, muted} (or null to clear, equivalent to mentions_only). Default invariant: payload.watcher_actor_id MUST equal envelope actor_id, unless writer holds cx.flow.watch.set.others. Cross-actor writes MUST carry refs[role=audit_pair] to a same-batch cx.audit.accessed event with access_kind=watch_set_others. The watches Relation (actor --watches--> flow) is a derived projection of this cell, not a separate truth source — direct cx.relation.create relation_kind=watches MUST schema_violation. See models/flow-and-message.md §8.
Space create (board / list / swimlane / calendar bucket / etc.)
Space metadata update (title, rank, kind-specific fields)

Space parent declaration. Parent is another cx:space: or null; cross-Realm parent is navigation only and never propagates Realm membership, capabilities, history, E2EE keys, retention, or federation policy.
Space archive (UI-level grouping archive; contained Flows MUST be relocated or follow archive)
Space restore (transition state archived -> active; only valid when current state == archived; tombstoned Spaces MUST NOT be restored)
Space tombstone (irreversible; contained Flows MUST be relocated before)
Message-scoped redaction; does not grant generic redaction authority
Generic redaction envelope for non-message objects/events and profile-declared content trimming

Morph schema_refs[] migration. First-class event for evolving a Morph's schema_refs[] without bypassing audit / capability gates. Carries (from_schema_refs[], to_schema_refs[], compatibility_class, migration_evidence?). Required capability cx.morph.schema.migrate (high risk tier; see capability-action-registry.json). compatibility_class = additive | breaking | transformation; core reducers MUST reject breaking/transformation unless the Realm declares cx.profile.morph.schema_migration_transformations.v1. See zh/models/morph.md §4.1 S3.

Morph business-progression stage transition. Single source of truth for mutating Morph.stage / Morph.stage_changed_at; cx.morph.update / cx.morph.schema_migrate patches on those paths MUST be rejected (forbidden-wire). The payload intentionally carries no reason / note / explanation field — rationale belongs in a Message on an associated discussion track that 'references' this event. Reducer enforces hard invariants from zh/models/common-fields.md §5.3.3: state=redacted yields failed_precondition reason=morph_already_terminal; state=archived yields morph_not_active; same-value self-transition is accepted but does NOT update stage_changed_at; reducer overwrites any wire-supplied stage_changed_at with the event's created_at.

Agent signing key authorization. Payload MUST validate as event-payload.schema.json#/$defs/agent_key_authorize_payload and bind agent_did, key_id, verification_method, accountable_actor, agent_key_scope, audience, issued_at, expires_at, and approval_evidence.
Agent signing key revocation. Payload MUST validate as event-payload.schema.json#/$defs/agent_key_revoke_payload and bind agent_did, key_id, revoked_at, revoked_by, and revocation_frontier.

Agent signing key rotation. Payload MUST validate as event-payload.schema.json#/$defs/agent_key_rotate_payload; key_id names the retiring key and replacement_key_id names the new key under the same accountable_actor with equivalent or narrower agent_key_scope.
Holder-private consent declaration: 'I consent to receive <consent_scope> from <peer>'
Revoke a previously granted consent (shares the cx.consent.grant cell; semantically a remove on the consent or_set)
Realm-scoped profile override. The event kind keeps the historical space_override spelling for wire compatibility; payload.target_realm_id is the target Realm and no Space boundary is created.

Push route binding for a (recipient_service_did, principal, device, push_route) tuple. Carries push_target_id, push_gateway_did, encryption_key, capabilities. Stored as actor-private state on the recipient Principal Server only; MUST NOT be replicated to Principal Servers outside the binding's recipient_service_did context.
MLS commit or Welcome processing failure diagnostic
Signed hard-erasure receipt. Attests deletion outcome and retained verification stub within an issuer-declared storage boundary; does not prove independent third-party copies disappeared.

Range-bound completeness attestation. Distinct from cx.audit.ryw_receipt (per-event read-your-writes hint) and cx.event_batch_receipt (set-bound integrity hint): this attestation asserts completeness over an explicit (from_frontier, to_frontier) + per-actor seq interval range. Issuer commits to having observed every reducer-input event in scope; witness quorum or independent anchor backing is required for non-self-attested deployments. See zh/sync/operations-sync.md §4.2.
Lift a previously anchored moderation decision

Submit an appeal against an existing cx.moderation.decision. Writes the appeal cell to state=submitted. Schema: cx.schema.moderation_appeal.v1. See zh/governance/content-moderation.md §5.5 (appeal flow).
Reviewer acknowledges the appeal and transitions cell state submitted → under_review. Identifies the reviewing actor and target appeal. Schema: cx.schema.moderation_appeal.v1.

Reviewer's verdict on the appeal: uphold (decision stands) / overturn (decision reversed, emits cx.moderation.decision.lift) / modify (decision adjusted). Transitions cell state under_review → decided. Schema: cx.schema.moderation_appeal.v1.

Closes the appeal after the decided window expires (default 30 days). Transitions cell state decided → closed; locks against re-appeal of the same target by the same appellant. Schema: cx.schema.moderation_appeal.v1.

Read cursor advance event (actor-private). Writes the actor's latest read position for a given (realm_id, read_scope) tuple. Was historically named cx.read.cursor; renamed to align the event_kind, capability action, schema id and typed ID prefix on a single noun root read_cursor.

Attested_hardware Audit Agent removal — enclave-signed attestation that historical epoch / exporter secrets held by the removed Audit Agent have been cryptographically destroyed. MUST be in the same anchor batch as the paired cx.mls.commit that removes the Audit Agent (see crypto-media/audited-e2ee.md §3.1.1). Wire schema versioning expressed via `requirements.features` (e.g. `cx.feature.audit_destruction_v1`), not via a `.v<n>` suffix on the kind name.

Forced downgrade of audit_assurance from attested_hardware to disclosed_policy when the required cx.audit.epoch_key_destruction attestation is not produced within the deadline; rewrites Realm audit policy and triggers UI banner. Wire schema versioning expressed via `requirements.features`.

schemas.description: Reference business-field schema used by the Morph type-system example. It validates the customer_risk fields.status / fields.severity payload carried inside cx.schema.morph.v1 containers.
Signed DID continuity / migration proof payload
Encrypted minimal-metadata binding from Realm-scoped pairwise DID to principal DID, scoped by realm_id and trust_domain.
Builder-side candidate object for Handle resolution intent=member_add | invite (identity-handles.md §3.7); produces a Realm-scoped member_delivery_binding only after Join Policy re-validation.
Schema-registry object for applet protocol metadata snapshots. Event payloads for cx.applet.* use typed payload definitions in event-payload.schema.json.
Schema-registry object for agent protocol metadata snapshots. Event payloads for cx.agent.* use typed payload definitions in event-payload.schema.json.
Signed hard-erasure receipt payload for cx.audit.erasure_receipt
Minimal retained verification stub bound by erasure-receipt.retained_stub_hash
Wire payload schema for cx.cross_signing.publish — establishes the PSK→{SSK, USK} binding on the principal control stream. See device-lifecycle.md §5.1.
Wire payload schema for cx.cross_signing.reset — retires the current (SSK, USK) generation under one of four kinds of high-risk proof. See device-lifecycle.md §14.1.
Structured Bottom (⊥) diagnostic surfaced on /account/subscribe, /events, and state query responses when a cell's effective Lattice value is undefined

Canonical ServiceDescribe response for cx.server.describe and per-surface describe operations: base service metadata plus claim-level partitions (supported_operations / implemented_features / claimed_profiles / verified_profiles / experimental_features / compat_surfaces). Enforces development_mode=true => verified_profiles=[]. See service-surface.md §3.0.

storage_rules: Protocol wire objects, canonical JSON, signatures, hashes, fixtures, logs, API DTOs, and cross-service references MUST use the full typed form cx:<kind>:<uuid> unless a special form below applies.

Storage implementations MAY store raw 16-byte UUID values (e.g. PostgreSQL `uuid` column) without the cx:<kind>: prefix when the table, column, or explicit kind field already supplies the type context.
Implementations that store raw IDs MUST restore the full typed form before computing canonical JSON, event IDs, payload hashes, detached proofs, federation payloads, sync cursors, or audit logs.
The <kind> segment is part of the signed/canonical wire value. It MUST NOT be changed, inferred differently, or stripped during verification, forwarding, backfill, or replay.

The UUID segment MUST be RFC 9562 UUID version 7 (48-bit Unix-millisecond timestamp + 4-bit version=7 + 12-bit rand_a + 2-bit variant=10b + 62-bit rand_b), serialized as the canonical 36-character lowercase hex form `xxxxxxxx-xxxx-7xxx-Nxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx` where N ∈ {8,9,a,b}.

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store as an opaque token or store server-private cursor state keyed by a raw token.
special_forms.description: Opaque sync/query cursor; not a typed-UUIDv7 object ID.

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store digest bytes/hex separately from any logical blob row ID.
special_forms.description: Content-addressed blob reference; distinct from cx:blob:<uuid> blob metadata IDs.

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store profile and raw profile_id separately.
special_forms.description: MLS-profile scoped reference such as KeyPackage IDs; validated by the E2EE profile, not by the generic typed-UUIDv7.

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store scope and random identifier separately when used in credential tables.
special_forms.description: Realm-scoped pseudonymous credential reference; validated by the E2EE profile. v1 core uses Realm as the boundary; Matrix-style Room terminology is only allowed in MIMI/Matrix interop modules.

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store as a content-addressed canonical Anchor hash.
Store canonical tuple fields separately when indexing cell state.
Store the scope string as an opaque deployment-level identifier; it appears in server describe, Realm policy, and high-risk proof transcripts.
special_forms.description: Deployment-scope trust domain identifier. Scope is a lowercase opaque label (alphanumerics, dot, dash, underscore, colon; max 128 chars). Used to prevent cross-deployment / cross-sovereign replay of high-risk proofs (e.g. cx.cross_signing.reset §14.1). NOT a typed-UUIDv7 object id. See identity-did.md §3.6.

id_kinds.description: Moderation appeal ID — opaque key for the cx.component.moderation_appeal.v1 cell. Created by cx.moderation.appeal.submit; referenced by review / decision / close events. See zh/governance/content-moderation.md §5.5.
Directory-local announce ingest record ID. It is typed and UUIDv7-shaped for validator consistency, but it is scoped to the issuing Directory and is not a global federated object authority.
Blob metadata row ID; content-addressed blobs use the special digest form
Abstract capability definition reference ID; signed grant objects use cx:grant:<uuid>.
Signed capability grant object ID used by cx.schema.capability.v1 and grant/revoke references.

Space object ID — structural grouping object inside a Realm (board, list, swimlane, calendar bucket, etc.). Authorization-transparent: never carries its own membership / policy / E2EE group; resolves to the containing Realm.
Realm object ID — security / sync / auth / E2EE boundary. Always carries membership, policy, history_visibility, MLS group binding, and federation policy.

operation_registry.description: Canonical operation catalog for generated service operation views and transport bindings.

generated_views.role: HTTP/OpenAPI binding shape aligned to the catalog; not a second operation namespace.
Descriptive operation map and governance notes; excerpt-only unless explicitly marked generated.

registry_rules: New operation_id values MUST be added here before any OpenAPI, HTTP binding table, SDK generator, or alternative transport binding references them.
Generated views MAY change shape, grouping, or field order, but MUST NOT introduce, rename, or remove operation_id values that are absent from this catalog.
Supporting Contrix core does not imply support for every registered operation. Implementations MUST advertise supported_operations and supported_profiles explicitly.

Each surface_groups entry carries a tier (see capability_tiers); only the core tier is implied by claiming v1 protocol support. Extension, interop_bridge, and deployment_local surfaces require explicit advertisement.

Profile matrices in artifacts/profiles/conformance-profiles.json define role-level MUST/SHOULD requirements; the surface groups below define machine-readable capability families for discovery, docs, and lint.

capability_tiers.core: Base interoperable surfaces implied by claiming Contrix v1 protocol support (service discovery, identity registry, events/account aggregate).
capability_tiers.extension: Optional interoperable surfaces that are part of the Contrix specification but require explicit discovery/profile advertisement.
capability_tiers.interop_bridge: Adapter surfaces that bridge Contrix to external protocols (MIMI Internet-Drafts, third-party Applet hosts). Implementations advertise these only when the external protocol is supported; bridge operations are not part of any core or extension profile and frequently mirror an in-spec operation via bridges_to.
capability_tiers.deployment_local: Deployment-specific, operator, or product-local surfaces that MUST NOT be assumed from core protocol support alone.

operations.notes: Issues a short-TTL, single-blob, read-only pre-signed URL whose authorization material rides in the URL itself (query string). Used as a deliberate carve-out of the no-credentials-in-URL rule (server-threat-model.md S21) so that browser primitives like /

HTTP-specific POST/body form of cx.events.query. Semantically identical (same selector / cursor / order / filter parameter set, same response shape). Choose when URL length would exceed practical limits (large realms[]/actors[] arrays, complex filters object) or when query parameters would be logged inadvertently by proxies. gRPC / MQ bindings reuse the canonical Events/Query — request body uses the same shape across all transports.
Dereference a known set of event_id / event_hash references to full EventEnvelope objects. Point lookup by identifier, not a range scan — use cx.events.query for selector-based reads.

Canonical broadcast ephemeral send operation for cx.schema.ephemeral_envelope.v1. Carries cx.presence, cx.typing, cx.receipt.read, and cx.call.signal; MUST NOT persist the signal as a durable Event or advance actor_seq / Realm frontier.
Canonical HTTP binding is POST /api/v1/policy/check (bare path inheriting the global /api/v1 prefix).
Extension read surface for reducer-maintained Flow lifecycle projection rows scoped by realm_id. This is a derived read model, not a canonical truth source.
Extension read surface for reducer-maintained Morph lifecycle projection rows scoped by realm_id. This is a derived read model, not a canonical truth source.
Extension read surface for reducer-maintained Space lifecycle projection rows scoped by realm_id. This is a derived read model, not a canonical truth source.

Streaming push of cross-Realm account-aggregate deltas (cross-Realm frontier, to_device queue, account_data, device_lists, presence, unread / notification counts). Connection is long-lived; server pushes NDJSON frames as new data becomes available. Symmetric with cx.events.subscribe — both are streaming subscriptions, differing only in scope (events.subscribe = per-Realm event log; account.subscribe = account-aggregate). Replaces the prior Matrix-derived long-poll cx.account.sync; not wire-compatible with Matrix /sync.

High-assurance optional endpoint to revoke a previously issued cursor authority. Revocation hits return cursor_revoked and MUST NOT advance to-device ack, account subscribe position, barrier wait, or dropped recovery state.

risk_tier_definitions.low: Read, projection, discovery, ack, and account-private affordances. Freshness fail-closed treats unknown / stale as local-pending allowed (capabilities.md §18).
risk_tier_definitions.medium: Object create / update / delete, message authoring, invite issuance, MLS proposal, audit query. Freshness requires recent frontier within freshness_required_ms.
risk_tier_definitions.high: Capability mutation, policy mutation, lifecycle freeze / tombstone / destroy, schema redefinition, MLS commit / welcome / genesis, audit export, moderation decision, admin / hierarchy / upgrade. Freshness MUST be within freshness_required_ms; partition forces local pending with no peer visibility.

registry_rules: Wire capability grant.actions[] entries MUST be drawn from this registry; wildcards / segment globs are statically rejected by capability-grant.schema.json.

Receivers MUST default to risk_tier=high when an action submitted in a grant or evaluated in policy is not present in this registry; this is the freshness fail-closed default required by capabilities.md §18.

required_constraints lists typed-constraint shorthand names that the capability evaluator MUST enforce for the action regardless of the grant author's declarations; absence in this list does NOT disable other declared constraints.

required_evaluator_checks lists non-grant-field invariants (for example actor_eq_target_author or audit_pair_required) that admission control MUST enforce from Event context, reducer state, or paired audit evidence. These are not grant-constraint schema fields.

target_event_kinds links the action to one or more cx.* event_kinds in event_kind_registry. Empty array means the action authorizes a read / projection / signaling path that does not produce a durable reducer-input event. Reducer admission for a listed event_kind MUST verify the actor holds at least one matching action grant.

profile is null for v1 core actions, or a cx.profile.*.v<n> id when the action is only meaningful inside that profile. Receivers without the named profile MUST treat the action as unknown (risk_tier=high default).
